rv.q: Eloise Pennycott’s script unfolds episodically: one year, Alana struggles with the basics of BSL; the next, the couple sign to each other with ease. From the outset, electricity runs between them, shown best in quiet sections of movement directed by Raffie Julien.

But unfortunately, the second act then completely undoes itself with a twist ending that goes unnecessarily meta, entirely ruining the story it had just been telling in order to hammer home its abundantly clear messagewhile casting the story to the side.
